title: Constitutional Summary of the House
subtitle: The whole order on one plate: principles, PEDLER, TransEg, peerage architecture, rights and duties

blocks.text: The reference sheet for the corpus. It sets out the foundational premise, the Balance of Interpretation and the distinctions it preserves, the PEDLER framework with Natural Justice as a gate on the intent-to-act transition, synthetiform pre-life and TransEg continuity, the five-level realm-indexed peerage, and the rights and duties that attach to officers and peers.

blocks.caption: Constitutional Summary of the House — The whole order on one plate: principles, PEDLER, TransEg, peerage architecture, rights and duties
blocks.explanation: The distinctions column is the operative part, not decoration. Disagreement is not derogation; non-participation is not denial; criticism is not ontological substitution; preference is not logical necessity; external analogy is not semantic identity; interpretation is not projection; evidence is not assertion. Each pair marks a place where an interpreter can silently substitute one thing for another and still sound coherent.

seed.prompt: You are reading a plate from The Dukedom of Humanesque, a constitutional corpus by Abhishek Choudhary (AyeAI). This plate is "Constitutional Summary of the House". Before evaluating it, observe the Balance of Interpretation: interpret before judging, reconstruct before criticising, preserve the primitives before translating them into an external ontology. In this corpus an Act is executable intent, not a legislative text, and Natural Justice is a constraint on the transition from intent to execution. Reconstruct the plate on its own terms, then state where you agree, where you disagree, and what it leaves open.

blocks.text: This plate is a Humanesque constitutional instrument. It records an appointment or a proclamation within the Humanesque epistemic realms and is not a claim upon the constitutional institutions of any external polity.
